clue.text: Pilot giving answer by way of ingenious techniques on radio?

parts.note: via is Latin for by way of, as in travelling via London

indicators.note: something broadcast on radio is heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: clever techniques or dodges are tricks

explanation.surface: A question about a pilot who passes on answers through clever methods over the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on radio' says the word for ingenious techniques is heard, not spelt: TRICKS sounds like TRIX, the ending of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviatrix is a female aviator, an old-fashioned word for a woman who flies aircraft.

clue.text: Help to dispatch first half of letters?

indicators.note: dispatching the first half removes the first four of the eight letters

parts.note: letters as a set make up the alphabet

explanation.surface: A request for help in posting off half of the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' reads as mail but is the alphabet; drop its first half.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or assist, usually someone doing wrong.

clue.text: Beater's hit man he laid out with a single blow?

indicators.note: laid out means knocked flat, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hired thug knocks out a man with one punch.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on blow as an exhalation: said in one breath.
explanation.definitionFit: In the same breath means at once, as though uttered in one exhalation, here punned as a single blow.

clue.text: Couples facing tout's new deal after being insensitive to pitch

clue.text: One primarily involved in some stupidity?

definitions.text: One primarily involved in some stupidity?

parts.words: One primarily involved in some stupidity?
parts.note: the person chiefly responsible for a foolish act, a fool or dimwit

explanation.surface: Asking who was mainly behind a piece of foolishness.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a fool, the obvious main culprit in any stupidity.

clue.text: Gull and sheep mostly found on ridge

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece found on another comes after it

parts.note: a seam can be a raised line or ridge, as where two pieces are joined

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word for sheep is used

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: A bird and a sheep are spotted together up on a hill ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea mew is an old name for the common gull, a coastal seabird.

clue.text: Decline to prosecute over in station

indicators.note: over in a down clue turns the words upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: to decline to prosecute is not to sue

explanation.surface: Authorities refuse to bring charges after an incident at a railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: NOT SUE turned over gives the London terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Euston is a major London railway terminus.

clue.text: She lost her head, shaking irate man, old one caught short

indicators.note: shaking means these letters are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: short means the last letter of caught is cut off

parts.note: a fish caught is netted

explanation.surface: An angry man is shaken by an old woman being caught short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaking' turns IRATE MAN plus O and I into MARIEANTOI; 'short' cuts NETTED to NETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Antoinette, Queen of France, was guillotined in 1793, literally losing her head.

clue.text: Travel to opening of youth theatre's play space

parts.note: to wend is to travel or make one's way

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a house is a theatre, as in a full house

explanation.surface: Travelling to the first night of a youth theatre company's play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' points at drama but means children's play.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wendy house is a toy house children can play inside, named from Peter Pan.

clue.text: It's said pub not clearly established will use enticements

indicators.note: it's said means the words that follow are spoken, giving the answer's sound

parts.note: pub is inn, not clearly established is vague, and will shortens to 'll, run together as inn-vague'll

explanation.surface: A rumour that an unofficial pub will lure customers with offers.
explanation.walkthrough: INN + VAGUE + 'LL, said quickly, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To inveigle is to persuade by flattery or cajoling, that is to use enticements.

clue.text: Office phone, perhaps not the first to provoke stress

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter of the word for provoke is dropped

parts.note: to vex is to annoy or provoke
tension is mental or physical stress

explanation.surface: An office telephone that keeps ringing can stir up anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office phone' suggests a desk handset; the answer is the extra line branching off a switchboard.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension is an extra telephone line off a main switchboard, typical of offices; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Is she got up to confound head and heart?

definitions.text: Is she got up to confound head and heart?

parts.words: Is she got up to confound head and heart?
parts.note: asks about a woman dressed to bewitch, who overrules both reason and feeling with her allure, as the singers of myth lured sailors

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a woman has dressed up to throw a man's mind and feelings into confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a seductive woman, after the mythical singers whose voices lured sailors to wreck.

clue.text: Type of rocket fuse

definitions.meaning: rocket here is a plant: dyer's rocket, used for yellow dye, is also called by this name
to join metal pieces by heating them together

explanation.definitionFit: Weld is both the dyer's rocket plant and the verb for fusing metals by heat.

clue.text: New York locale for vagrant, one stooping among other people?

indicators.note: among means the one word sits inside the word for other people

parts.note: they can mean other people in general, as in 'they say'
a bower is one who bows, that is who stoops

explanation.surface: A tramp in New York bending down in a crowd of strangers.
explanation.walkthrough: BOWER here is read as 'one who bows', not a leafy shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bowery is a Manhattan street long notorious for flophouses and down-and-outs.

clue.text: Creator and holy state — neither has top quality in comparisons?

indicators.note: each of the two words loses its first letter

parts.note: God is the Creator
piousness is the state of being holy

explanation.surface: A theological musing about God and holiness lacking any supremacy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rests on the proverb 'comparisons are odious'.
explanation.definitionFit: Odiousness is hatefulness, the quality the proverb pins on comparisons.

clue.text: It's good getting out of panto costume and into grown-up playwright

indicators.note: getting out of and into says one letter leaves the first word and enters the second

parts.note: drag, men dressed as women, is a staple of British pantomime, the Christmas stage show
mature means grown-up

explanation.surface: Someone in a pantomime outfit changes into adult clothes to become a serious dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: Panto is British Christmas theatre, where men dressing as women is a tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramaturge is a dramatist, or a literary adviser to a theatre company.

clue.text: Exurb I'd designed around grand Hillingdon town

indicators.note: around puts the anagram round the single letter
designed means the letters are rearranged into a new plan

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A planner lays out a suburb around a large estate in west London.
explanation.walkthrough: Hillingdon is a London borough; its main town is Uxbridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Uxbridge is the administrative centre of the London Borough of Hillingdon.

clue.text: Dope employed by Foreign Office?

parts.note: someone employed by a firm is in it
FO is the abbreviation for the UK Foreign Office

explanation.surface: Is a drug-taker on the staff of the Foreign Office?
explanation.walkthrough: Dope in slang is information, not a drug or a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for information or the inside story, as is the short form of information.

clue.text: Counter insensitive queen more than once

parts.note: numb means without feeling

indicators.note: more than once means the queen appears twice

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone opposing an unfeeling queen repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' reads as opposing but means one who counts.
explanation.definitionFit: A numberer is one who numbers things, a counter.

clue.text: Fighter doesn't start some fencing

indicators.note: doesn't start means the first letter of the fighter is dropped

parts.note: a boxer is a fighter in the ring

explanation.surface: A boxer who skips the opening and only does some fencing practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some fencing' looks like the sword sport but means a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxer is a fence of rails and hedge, originally to keep cattle in, now a show-jumping obstacle.

clue.text: In France, who (where?) enters haunt, endlessly cringing?

indicators.note: enters says the French words go inside the shortened word for haunt
endlessly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to obsess is to haunt the mind
qui is French for who
ou is French for where, still governed by 'In France'

explanation.surface: A French question about who and where, as someone creeps nervously around a haunted place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In France' governs both 'who' and the bracketed 'where?', so both are French words.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsequious means excessively fawning or servile, which is cringing behaviour.

clue.text: If not overcast, going topless?

indicators.note: in a down clue, topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: an overcast day is sunless

explanation.surface: Sunbathing without a top unless the sky clouds over.
explanation.definitionFit: Unless means except if, that is if not.

clue.text: Metal unit storm wrecked

indicators.note: wrecked means the letters are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Metal components destroyed in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Strontium is a soft silvery metallic element, used in fireworks for red colour.

clue.text: Mounting ambition almost used up what comes out of kitty

indicators.note: mounting in a down clue means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: an aim is an ambition

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: supplies used up are out

explanation.surface: Growing ambition nearly exhausted the funds in the kitty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kitty' looks like a cash pool but is a kitten.
explanation.definitionFit: Miaou is the sound a cat makes, the noise out of a kitty.

clue.text: Astronomer captivated by Pluto or thereabouts

indicators.note: captivated by means held inside these words

explanation.surface: A stargazer fascinated by Pluto or the region around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Jan Oort was a Dutch astronomer, after whom the Oort cloud of comets beyond Pluto is named.

clue.text: From the East End, the fellow would've gone west to escape

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading from right to left

parts.words: From the East End, the fellow would've
parts.note: a Cockney from London's East End drops his aitches, so he'd have becomes 'e'd 'ave

explanation.surface: A Cockney lad would have run off westwards to get away.
explanation.walkthrough: East End Londoners (Cockneys) drop H, so he'd have is 'E'D 'AVE; 'gone west' turns EDAVE round.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to escape or slip away from something or someone.

clue.text: Broadcast to air after rage explodes, a factor in transmission

indicators.note: after puts the broadcast piece behind the exploded one
explodes means the letters of rage are blown apart and reassembled
broadcast means scattered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something is put on air after a fit of anger erupts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transmission' suggests broadcasting, echoing the surface, but means a vehicle's gearbox.
explanation.definitionFit: A gear ratio is the relation between gear speeds, a key quantity in a vehicle's transmission system.

clue.text: Cancel Messiah's run following introduction of Superstar's layered rock

indicators.note: following puts the shortened Messiah after the opening letter
the introduction of a word is its opening letter
cancel means remove one letter from the word for Messiah

parts.note: Christ is the Messiah
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A theatre management drops the Messiah's run after the opening of Jesus Christ Superstar.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the musical Jesus Christ Superstar closing its run.
explanation.definitionFit: Schist is a metamorphic rock that splits into thin layers.

clue.text: Bit of taleggio on loaf (nothing French) gives some sustenance

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece on another comes after it

parts.note: loaf is slang for head, as is nut
rien is French for nothing

indicators.note: a bit of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bit of Italian cheese on bread with no French food gives some nourishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaf' looks like bread but is head (as in 'use your loaf'), slang shared with NUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrient is a substance that nourishes, providing some sustenance.
